methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $144M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 1 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Atomic Machines is a Series A-stage semiconductor company founded by Jeff Holden that has raised $144M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public semiconductor peers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers including SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, and Credo Semiconductor.

Given data limitations, only one valuation method proved applicable: stage-progression analysis. Using total raised ($144M) as a proxy for post-money valuation and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A progression to the next stage, this method implies a valuation of $288M. A sensitivity range of ±15% yields a low of $245M and a high of $331M.

The peer-median approach could not be applied due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables in the Chips & Semiconductors sector; while 12 same-sector peers exist, fewer than three matched simultaneous filters for stage, adjacent valuation tier, and funding recency. Public-comp anchoring (median P/S of 21.5x across the three public comps) remains inapplicable absent the target's revenue disclosure. The analysis therefore rests on a single methodological pillar. Key uncertainties include the target's actual revenue run rate, recent funding terms, and comparative burn dynamics relative to the peer set. A more robust triangulation would require either disclosure of financial metrics or access to recent institutional term sheets from comparable Series A rounds.
